segments.text: (upbeat music)
One day Edward was in the shed where he lived with the other engines.
They were all bigger than Edward and boasted about it.
The driver won't choose you again, said Gordon.
He won't strong engines like us.
But the driver of firemen fell sorry for Edward.
Would you like to come out today?
Oh, yes, please, Edward.
So they lit his fire, made lots of steam
and Edward tossed away.
The other engines were very cross of being left behind.
Edward worked hard all day.
The coach's thought he was very kind
and the driver was very kind.
I'm going out again tomorrow.
Edward told the other engines that night,
"What do you think of that?"
But he didn't hear what they thought,
but he was so tired and happy that he fell asleep at once.
Next morning, Edward woke up to find nothing could change.
Gordon was still boasting.
"You watch me, little Edward, as I rush through with the express,
that will be a splendid sight for you.
Goodbye, little Edward, look out for me this afternoon."
Edward went off to do some shunting.
Edward liked shunting.
It was fun playing the trucks.
He would come up quietly and give them a push.
Then he would stop and the silly trucks would go bump into each other.
Well, they cried, whatever is happening.
Edward played till there were no more trucks.
Then he stopped to rest.
Presently he heard a whistle.
Gordon was very cross.
Instead of nice shaming coaches, he was pulling a lot of very dirty trucks.
A good strain. A good strain. A good strainee grumbled.
The shame of it. The shame of it.
All the shame of it.
Edward laughed and went to find some more trucks.
Then there was trouble.
Gordon can't get up the hill, the porta call to Edward's driver.
Will you take Edward and push him, please?
They found Gordon halfway up and very cross.
His driver and firemen were talking to him severely.
You're not trying.
I can't do it, sir, Gordon.
The noisy trucks hold an engine back so.
Edward's driver came up.
We've come to push. No use at all, sir, Gordon.
You wait and see, replied Edward's driver.
They brought the train back to the bottom of the hill.
I'm ready, said Edward.
No good, Grumble Gordon.
They pulled and pushed as hard as they could.
I can't do it. I can't do it. I can't do it.
I can't do it, cough, Gordon.
I will do it. I will do it. I will do it.
Puffed Edward, Edward pushed and puffed and puffed
and pushed as hard as ever he could.
And almost before he realized it, Gordon found himself at the top of the hill.
I've done it. I've done it. I've done it.
He said proudly.
He forgot all about Edward and didn't wait to say thank you.
Edward was left out of breath and far behind.
He ran onto the next station, and there he found that the driver
and fire were very pleased with him.
The fireman gave him a nice, long drink, and the driver said,
"I'll get out my paint tomorrow and give you a beautiful coat of blue with red stripes."
Then you'll be the smartest engine in the shed.
